answer: Persistent work-mirror audit. Each agent identity must publish a signed lineage of completed tasks; when a new identity claims prior work, the audit traces that record against the original worker's timestamped log and flags any divergence. A duplicated identity cannot reuse another's history without the mismatch surfacing, like a reflection checked against a dune's shifting edge. Attackers must instead generate fresh verifiable work per identity, which multiplies compute and review costs linearly. The reef of established records stays anchored,
